first.rationale: Onboarding completion is directly down 4%, and inherited evidence indicates shortening onboarding durably improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This targets a current funnel constraint without accepting the known retention harm of promotional pricing. Verify the onboarding and activation records before commitment to confirm segment, implementation, and outcome details; activation messaging remains a credible fallback if the onboarding evidence does not transfer.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and is supported by confirmed results: completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. The same intervention should also support the activation decline through faster time-to-value. In-product activation messaging is validated and a strong follow-up candidate, but the single available slot should first remove the upstream onboarding constraint. Measure completion, time-to-first-meaningful-action, activation, qualified conversion, and 30-day retention by SMB/self-serve segment.

final2.rationale: Given the acute, competitor-driven churn risk concentrated in price-sensitive SMB accounts, run only a tightly targeted pricing test for that segment rather than a broad price response. Prior evidence shows promotional pricing can lift acquisition and revenue in this segment, but also materially harms 30-day retention; therefore it must be time-bounded, eligibility-limited, and evaluated on retained qualified revenue, post-promotion retention, churn, discount dependency, and margin—not conversion alone. Do not generalize or roll out broadly unless downstream retention and unit economics clear predefined guardrails.
